blocks.text: KING OF JUDAH · TWO KINGDOMS
Amaziah. Twenty-nine years in Jerusalem; victor over Edom, beaten by Israel.
REIGNEDi
29 years c. 796–767 BC (dates vary)
CAPITAL
Jerusalem
HOUSE
House of David 9th of 20 in Judah
VERDICT
✓ Did right “And he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD, yet not like David his father”
PROPHETS
A man of God (unnamed) · A prophet (unnamed)
JUDAH (THE SOUTH): 20 RULERS REHOBOAM → ZEDEKIAH
SUCCESSION
The two kingdoms
THE VERDICT
How Scripture judges the reign
“And he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD, yet not like David his father”
2 Kings 14:3 (KJV) →
“he did according to all things as Joash his father did”
2 Kings 14:3 (KJV) →
BUT ALSO
But also: "the high places were not taken away". 2 Kings 14:4
Chronicles adds that he brought back the gods of Edom, bowed down to them, and silenced the prophet who rebuked him. 2 Chronicles 25:14–16
CHRONICLES GIVES IT AS
“And he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD, but not with a perfect heart.”
2 Chronicles 25:2 (KJV) →
JUDAH (THE SOUTH): 20 RULERS
✓ Did right ✕ Did evil ◐ Mixed ● No verdict formula
THE KINGDOM
Jerusalem and the places of the reign
Judah (the south) · tribe of Judah. Only places Scripture names are shown, each where the Atlas puts it.
EVENTS
Wars, works and turning points
UNDATED IN SCRIPTURE
THE NATION
What the nation did
The people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places. 2 Kings 14:4
Edom's gods worshipped by the king (Chronicles). 2 Chronicles 25:14
PROPHETS
Prophets of the reign
Am A man of God (unnamed) “The LORD is able to give thee much more than this.”
Ap A prophet (unnamed) “Why hast thou sought after the gods of the people, which could not deliver their own people out of thine hand?”
ON THE WORLD STAGE
The powers of the day
ISRAEL
Jehoash (Joash) · Jeroboam II
TWO ACCOUNTS
Where Kings and Chronicles differ
Each ribbon joins the two accounts of one matter, passage to passage.
Why he lost to Israel
2 KINGS
2 CHRONICLES
Where he was buried
2 KINGS
2 CHRONICLES
Only in Chronicles
2 KINGS
2 CHRONICLES
DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
29 years (2 Kgs 14:2). Scripture gives lengths and cross-dates, never BC years.
THIELE, REVISED BY MCFALL (1991)
Printed form: 796–767 (PDF p. 23).
YOUNG (2005), REVISING THIELE
Printed form: 796–767 (p. 246 (Table 2)).
ALBRIGHT (1945)
Printed form: c. 800–783 (p. 21).
TRADITIONAL DATES (USSHER, 1658)
Printed form: 839–810 (p. 51-52 (scan leaf n30)).
Chronicles drew on other histories
C. F. Keil (1872); Ellicott's commentary
Chronicles supplements Kings from independent sources, and these details explain the later war with Israel. 2 Chronicles 25:6–16 [14][41]
A principle applied to history
E. Bertheau and O. Thenius (as reported by C. F. Keil and Ellicott, who reject it)
The idolatry was inferred from Amaziah's defeat rather than drawn from a record. 2 Chronicles 25:20 [13][41]
A known ancient policy
C. F. Keil (1872); W. E. Barnes (1899)
Conquerors sought to win over the gods of a conquered people; Solomon's shrines are an earlier example. 1 Kings 11:7 [13][149]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 4
2 Kings 12 2 Kings 14 2 Chronicles 24 2 Chronicles 25
PASSAGES · 5
2 Kings 12:21 2 Kings 14:1–22 2 Kings 14:23 2 Chronicles 24:27 2 Chronicles 25:1–28
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not say whether Amaziah was released by Jehoash or how long he was held.
Scripture does not say who led the conspiracy against him.

links.text: Athaliah, Queen who reigned over Judah, 6 years
